story:
“—Julius, got a sec?”

Hearing that voice call out through the window, Julius Juukulius lifted his face from his paperwork, adjusted the position of his glasses, and walked over to the window.

Through the slightly open ground-floor exterior window facing the garden—for ventilation purposes—a delicate-looking figure was peeking into the room.

“What’s the matter, Lady Anastasia? Weren’t you supposed to be heading out at this hour to inspect the markets with Mimi and the others?”

“That was the plan, but I ended up canceling. There’s somethin’ I wanna ask of you, Julius.”

“Of me?”

In the gardens of the Juukulius estate in the royal capital, Julius’s brows furrowed ever so slightly at the words of his liege, who had stuck out her tongue just a bit.

Then, coming to an understanding, he replied, “Understood,”

“I’ll prepare right away. I’ll go change, so please give me just a moment.”

“Huh, really? You don’t hafta change or nothin’—you’re fine as you are, aren’t ya?”

“Not at all. I can’t have you embarrassed in front of Lady Anastasia, so I must hurry and—”

“Embarrassed? C’mon, ain’t nobody around to see, so you’re makin’ a big deal outta nothin’.”

“No, Lady Anastasia—countless eyes are watching your every move. Even the slightest lapse in vigilance could become a vulnerability.”

Shaking his head slowly from side to side, Julius thus gently admonished his liege for her rashness. In response, Anastasia seemed not so much contrite as puzzled—“Hm?”—as she let out a curious little hum from that slender throat of hers, and then,

“Wait a minute—are you tryin’ to come along as my escort in Mimi and the others’ place, Julius?”

“—? Is that not the case?”

“Nah, that’s not it at all—I was thinkin’ our conversation wasn’t clickin’.”

Covering her mouth with her hand and letting out a tinkling laugh, Anastasia pointed out his mistake with a smile, and Julius reflected deeply on it.

Misreading his liege’s intentions, and on top of that offering utterly off-base advice—it was piling shame on top of shame.

And yet—,

“You’re so serious, Julius. That’s exactly why you’re perfect for my camp.”

“I’m not sure that feels much like a compliment.”

“Why not? I’m praisin’ ya left and right here. ‘When your pocket change matches the bill’—it’s a Hououin quotation.”

Declaring this proudly with her chest puffed out, Anastasia often borrowed words like these from great figures of the past in this way. —The quotations left behind by “Hououin of the Wastelands” tended toward the practical, and precisely for that reason, they sank deep into the soul and struck at the heart. Even now, they were said to fit the Anastasia camp like a glove—and indeed, they sank deep into Julius’s soul and struck at his heart.

That said, if he let it show too plainly on his face, he couldn’t claim to be fulfilling his duty as a knight, or so Julius thought. And so, keeping his expression calmly composed on the surface,

“That is far too great an honor,”

he replied, leaving it at that—though it was undoubtedly his true feelings.

“But if it’s not as a stand-in for Mimi and the others, then what business do you have with me? You said you had a request.”

“Right, right, almost forgot the main point. Y’see, I wanna borrow a bit of the power from your quasi-spirits’ kids.”

“The buds’?”

Raising an eyebrow at the unexpected request.

Quasi-spirits were the six spirits contracted to Julius—each of them enchanting him with their different scintillating qualities and possibilities, beautiful and valiant maidens all.

“Too much to ask?”

“If it weren’t at Lady Anastasia’s behest, they wouldn’t so easily nod yes, I imagine.”

“Oh? Well then, it was worth it to participate in the royal selection and make you my knight.”

“That too is a most generous assessment.”

It was enough to make him want to throw that earlier “over-the-top” judgment right back at her.

In any case, it was a request from Anastasia. Considering it no small matter, Julius steeled himself, nodded, and said, “Understood.”

“If that is your wish, Lady Anastasia, I shall respond with all my spirit.”

“As expected—reliable as ever. That’s why you’re the ‘foremost.’”

“So, what would you have of my buds?”

“Well, here’s the thing, though—”

As Anastasia beckoned him closer, Julius leaned out through the window and tilted his head to catch her voice. Parting the hair at his ear, exposing it, Julius drew near—and Anastasia brought her thin lips close to it, and spoke.

What she said was—,

“—Mind if I get you to whip up a little tornado?”

△▼△▼△▼△

To the stunned Julius, Anastasia explained in a rapid patter, her face still mischievous, complete with gestures.

According to her explanation, it went like this.

“Y’see, back when I’d only just met Mimi and the others, there was this street stall sellin’ a whole ton of paper balloons. They were these cute ones painted with pictures and colors and stuff, but then a little gust of wind came whippin’ through the street, and whoosh—they all went flyin’ up into the air!”

“That... must have been quite the ordeal for the stall’s owner.”

“That’s not the point! C’mon, picture the scene for me, would ya? It was spectacular—absolutely spectacular! The whole sky got filled up with paper balloons.”

Spreading her arms wide, Anastasia expressed that感動 with her whole body.

Fundamentally thoughtful and rational as she was, she would occasionally show this childish, childlike side of her—a return to innocence. It usually happened around those she was close to, like Ricardo, but the fact that she showed it to Julius too made him want to think of it as a sign of trust.

At any rate, the wonder and thrill of that scene came through loud and clear.

“So then, Lady Anastasia—you’d like to recreate that spectacle.”

“Exactly! I mean, can you believe it? Mimi and the others totally forgot about it. Sure, they were little back then, but still—no way.”

“There’s something heartbreaking about being forgotten, isn’t there? The more you cherish someone, the more a treasured memory matters.”

“Exactly. So that’s why I decided to... well, not just remind ‘em—I’m gonna layer a new memory on top.”

“Layer on top?”

“Better to make new memories than to keep hearin’ ‘I don’t remember’ over and over, and then if they remember the old one later, that’s just a bonus, right?”

“I see. How very like you, Lady Anastasia.”

Nodding at that, Julius turned his gaze out the window, to the estate’s gardens beyond Anastasia. Hearing her story now, the reason she’d called out to him from the garden made perfect sense.

“The paper balloons are with Mimi and the others?”

“Yeah, and Ricardo and Joshua are helpin’ out too. It’s an all-hands effort for the camp.”

“Then I’ve no choice but to lend my power as well.”

“Right? So, I’ll be waitin’—hold up.”

She cut herself off midsentence, her eyes going wide.

It was because Julius had gripped the window frame, given a light leap, vaulted straight out of the room’s window, and landed in the garden.

And then, extending a hand to his round-eyed liege,

“Time’s a-wastin’. Let’s hurry. Your earlier description has me wanting to see that sight for myself, Lady Anastasia.”

“Mmph, you and your cheeky little...”

“Lady Anastasia?”

“Nothin’. Alright then, shall we?”

Taking the hand he’d offered, Anastasia tilted her head. In response, Julius took hers and started walking.

As they walked along, Anastasia looked up at his profile, her lips forming the word “Julius,”

“And it’s not just Mimi and them—I wanted to make new memories with you too. So don’t you forget, alright?”

“————”

Remembering his own words from moments ago, Julius felt a flush of embarrassment and joy, and a great many other uplifting emotions besides, filling him to the brim as he nodded. “Yes.”

“I won’t forget. —I never will.”

That day, countless paper balloons danced into the skies above the Juukulius estate’s gardens, accompanied by a chorus of delighted cheers. —And true to his declaration, Julius Juukulius would treasure it as a precious memory, never to forget, holding it close in his heart forever.
